name: Marauder I

photos.alt: The Marauder I team stands with the completed red airframe under the Launch Canada tent, McMaster 23 lettering visible.
Marauder I stands vertical on the rail in the sandy clearing before launch.
A rocket leaves the pad with a visible exhaust plume at Launch Canada 2022.

summary: The first vehicle the team ever flew, and the one that proved we could get off the pad at all.
build: Marauder I was the team's first competition vehicle, built for Launch Canada's 10k COTS division in 2022. A 6 in fiberglass airframe with in-house structures, dual-deploy recovery, and student avionics, it carried McMaster 23 lettering on the pad. The rocket left the rail cleanly; we never recovered the airframe from the bush. The flight still proved the team could integrate subsystems and get off the pad.

name: Marauder II

photos.alt: The Marauder II team holds the airframe at Spaceport America Cup 2023, bib 55 and McMaster lettering readable.
Marauder II stands vertical on the desert launch rail, bib 55.
The recovered Marauder II airframe lies on the desert floor after landing.

specs.recovery: 2 ft drogue @ apogee · 12 ft main @ 1300 ft

build: Marauder II was the team's first Spaceport America Cup vehicle: a 5 in fiberglass airframe with clipped-delta fins, dual-deploy recovery, and an SRAD avionics suite flying as backup to COTS altimeters. It flew on a CTI M2150 (7,455 N·s).

name: Luminis

photos.alt: The Luminis team holds the completed airframe under a tent at the Spaceport America Cup pad area.
Luminis lies horizontal on the rail cradle, bib 58 legible, while the team makes final checks before launch.
A rocket climbs from the pad with a smoke trail, spectators watching from the range.
A team member kneels beside the recovered Luminis airframe, bib 58 visible, with parachute and hardware laid out on the ground.

summary: The first airframe designed around its payload rather than the other way round.

specs.recovery: 2 ft drogue @ apogee · 12 ft main @ 1400 ft

build: Luminis kept the 5 in fiberglass layout from Marauder II (Von Karman nose, three clipped-delta carbon fins) and added the team's first functional payload: an onboard camera for flight video. Dual-deploy recovery used a COTS EasyMini with Void Lake 4 as SRAD backup. It flew on a CTI 6800M3700-P (6,800 N·s).

name: Luminis V2

photos.alt: The full Luminis V2 team holds the completed airframe at the Launch Canada 2024 site, LUMINIS lettering and sponsor logos legible.
Luminis V2 stands vertical on the pad against clear sky, team members beside it for scale.
Luminis V2 climbs from the pad with a visible exhaust trail against the treeline.
The team gathers around the recovered Luminis V2 airframe on the ground after landing.

summary: The first vehicle we flew with a flight computer we trusted enough to publish the numbers.
build: Luminis V2's Launch Canada 2024 flight was the team's first fully nominal launch and recovery. Blue Raven flew as primary with EasyMini and Void Lake (VLF4) as backups. VLF4 came back flight-proven. The payload camera recorded the full flight. Apogee was 10,564 ft, 5.2% below the projected 11,146 ft.

name: Nimbus

photos.alt: The Nimbus team with disassembled airframe sections under the McMaster Engineering tent at Launch Canada 2025, NIMBUS lettering visible.
photos.caption: Integration at the range — the full crew with the airframe broken down for transport.

photos.alt: A team member arms Nimbus on the launch rail against clear sky before flight.
photos.caption: Arming on the rail. Last checks on pyrotechnics and avionics before the count.

photos.alt: The open avionics bay on the yellow Nimbus airframe, wiring and flight hardware visible.
photos.caption: The avionics stack wired into the bay — flight computers, harnesses, and bulkhead connectors.

photos.alt: Signed Nimbus fin sections on a towel after recovery, team names in gold marker.
photos.caption: Signed fins after recovery. Every flight crew leaves their mark before the airframe goes back in the rack.

summary: First place in the Payload Challenge and third in the Basic Launch Category at Launch Canada 2025.
build: Nimbus flew as a single-stage, commercial-motor airframe: 101.6 mm (4 in) in diameter, with a stability margin of 3.11 calibers. It flew on a CTI N1800, rated for 10,366.9 Ns of total impulse and 1,759.8 N of average thrust. Blue Raven flew as primary with EasyMini and Void Lake as backups. Dual-deploy recovery fired drogue near apogee and main at 1,496 ft AGL. Peak velocity was 1,254.98 ft/s (Mach 1.14 at burnout).

name: Osiris

photos.alt: Four team members hold the assembled Osiris airframe, OSIRIS lettering and bib number 25 visible, at the competition venue.
The open airframe before final assembly: left to right, the airbrake actuator, the avionics bay, and the payload section.
The team stands beside Osiris, vertical on the rail, before launch.
The recovery team in the bush, holding the recovered airframe sections beside the caught parachute.

summary: Our highest and fastest vehicle to date.

specs.recovery: 3 ft drogue @ apogee · 10 ft main @ 1500 ft

build: Osiris introduced two firsts for the team: functional airbrakes, and a student-designed flight computer that had already been flight-tested before competition, so we could fly it as a backup with confidence. The 101.6 mm (4 in) minimum-diameter airframe used fiberglass tubes rolled in-house, with carbon fibre tip-to-tip fin layups. It flew on a CTI O3400 (21,062 N·s), the most powerful motor in team history.
